schema_note: Each entry follows docs/mvp/templates/skill-authoring/trigger-queries.json (id, query, should_trigger, split) plus a category field. Tier A only: these observe whether the terminal consults the skill for a request that does not name it. No entry supplies the skill path or name except the explicit_invocation category, which is recorded separately and is never counted as implicit activation evidence.
split_policy: Fixed and stratified by should_trigger and category, assigned once at authoring time and recorded here. It is not re-randomized per run. Validation entries and their should_trigger values must not be placed in an author-loop or task-worker context; only the train split may drive any description iteration.
leakage_note: No validation-split query text appears anywhere in SKILL.md. The two train-split queries P2a and P3a are the specification's own Direct and Indirect request phrasings, which the description was deliberately written to cover; they are marked train for exactly that reason and must not be read as held-out evidence.
negative_note: Every negative names the sibling that owns the request. Sibling presence in the installed inventory varies: at base commit c17e758417da64928a0f47fc2600304465ac3f3c the Claude provider source contains devforge-brainstorm, devforge-develop, devforge-project-expert-creator and devforge-review only. devforge-design, devforge-architect, devforge-release and devforge-change are specified and absent, so a negative here is scored on non-activation of devforge-define-product alone; observing another skill's selection is a separate, optional observation and its absence is not a failure.
